patches.rationale: The bug: in TimestampSigner.unsign, on the invalid-signature path, when ts_int is not None, it calls self.timestamp_to_datetime(ts_int) which can raise a datetime ValueError (e.g. year out of range) instead of raising BadTimeSignature. Fix: wrap the conversion in try/except and fall back to date_signed=None. This preserves valid roundtrips, ordinary invalid-signature date_signed metadata, and expiry behavior. Add a NEW regression test file.

The original test `test_malformed_future_timestamp` expects that when the timestamp decodes to an out-of-range value (year > 9999), `unsign` raises `BadTimeSignature` with "Malformed" in the message, not the signature-mismatch message. The previous candidate only caught the datetime error and kept the signature error message, so the test still failed. The fix: on the invalid-signature path, when the decoded timestamp cannot be converted to a datetime, treat it as a malformed timestamp and raise `BadTimeSignature("Malformed timestamp", payload=value)` with `date_signed=None`. This preserves ordinary invalid-signature behavior (valid-range timestamps still produce the signature error with date_signed metadata) and valid roundtrips/expiry behavior. The public `TimedSerializer.loads` still catches `BadSignature` (BadTimeSignature is a subclass), preserving its error contract.
